ncertReference.chapter: Section 11: Rate Problems, LCM Efficiency & Relative Velocities

thirtySecondSummary: Rate-based arithmetic connects three major pillars: Averages (mean, weighted average, inclusion/replacement), Time & Work (LCM efficiency method, pipes & cisterns), and Speed, Time & Distance (relative speed, trains, boats & streams).
Average Formula: Average = (Sum of observations) / (Number of observations). When an old member is replaced: New Age = Old Age + (Change in Average * Total Count).
Time & Work LCM Method: Total Work = LCM of individual times. Individual efficiency = Total Work / Individual time. Time together = Total Work / Combined efficiency.
Speed, Time & Distance: Speed = Distance / Time. Conversion factor: km/h to m/s = Multiply by 5/18; m/s to km/h = Multiply by 18/5.
Average Speed: For two equal distances traveled at speeds u and v: Average Speed = 2uv / (u + v).
Relative Speed: Opposite directions = Add speeds (u + v); Same direction = Subtract speeds (u - v).

coreConcepts.title: Averages: Weighted Average and Inclusion/Replacement Shortcuts
coreConcepts.explanation:
Formulas for computing means and handling shifts in group compositions:
1. Weighted Average: When group 1 of size n1 has average A1 and group 2 of size n2 has average A2:
  - Combined Average A = (n1*A1 + n2*A2) / (n1 + n2).
2. Inclusion Shortcut:
  - When a new person joins a group of n members and increases the average by Δ:
  - New Member Value = Old Average + (n + 1) * Δ.
3. Replacement Shortcut:
  - When a member of weight W_old is replaced by a new person, changing average of n members by Δ:
  - W_new = W_old ± (n * Δ).
keyTakeaways: Replacement formula: New = Old ± (Total Count * Change in Average).
Weighted average combines distinct groups proportionally.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: CUET Quantitative Aptitude, Averages & Weighted Means, pp. 378-388.

coreConcepts.title: Time & Work and Pipes & Cisterns (The LCM Efficiency Technique)
coreConcepts.explanation:
The fastest method to solve Time & Work without fractions:
1. LCM Efficiency Method:
  - If A completes work in 10 days and B in 15 days:
  - Assume Total Work = LCM(10, 15) = 30 units.
  - Daily work of A (Efficiency) = 30 / 10 = 3 units/day.
  - Daily work of B (Efficiency) = 30 / 15 = 2 units/day.
  - Combined Efficiency = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day.
  - Time taken together = 30 / 5 = 6 days.
2. Work & Wages: Wages are divided in the ratio of work done (which equals ratio of efficiencies if time is equal).
3. Pipes & Cisterns:
  - Inlet pipes contribute positive efficiency (+units/hr); Outlet/leak pipes contribute negative efficiency (-units/hr).
keyTakeaways: Always assume Total Work = LCM of individual days.
Time Together = Total Work / Sum of Efficiencies.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: CUET Reasoning & Math Guide, Work, Efficiency & Pipes, pp. 390-402.

coreConcepts.title: Speed, Time & Distance: Trains and Boats & Streams
coreConcepts.explanation:
Motion under relative frames of reference:
1. Unit Conversion:
  - 1 km/h = 1000m / 3600s = 5/18 m/s.
  - To convert km/h to m/s: multiply by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h: multiply by 18/5.
2. Average Speed:
  - Total Distance / Total Time.
  - If two equal distances are traveled at speeds x and y: Avg Speed = 2xy / (x + y).
3. Train Crossing Models:
  - Crossing a point/pole: Distance = Length of train (L_t).
  - Crossing a platform/bridge: Distance = L_t + Length of platform (L_p).
4. Boats and Streams:
  - Speed of boat in still water = u; Speed of stream = v.
  - Downstream Speed (D) = u + v
  - Upstream Speed (U) = u - v
  - Boat speed u = (D + U) / 2; Stream speed v = (D - U) / 2.
keyTakeaways: Average Speed for equal halves = 2xy / (x + y).
Boat speed u = (D + U)/2; Stream speed v = (D - U)/2.
coreConcepts.ncertPointer: CUET Quantitative Aptitude, Kinematics & Relative Velocity, pp. 404-414.

workedExamples.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 18 days respectively. They worked together for 4 days, after which A left. In how many more days will B finish the remaining work alone?
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Determine Total Work = LCM(12, 18) = 36 units.

Step 2: Calculate daily efficiencies:
  - Efficiency of A = 36 / 12 = 3 units/day.
  - Efficiency of B = 36 / 18 = 2 units/day.
  - Combined efficiency (A + B) = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day.
Step 3: Work done in the first 4 days = 4 * 5 = 20 units.
Step 5: Time taken by B alone to finish remaining work = 16 / 2 = 8 days.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: LCM eliminates all fractional arithmetic, making Time & Work questions error-free.

workedExamples.question: A train 150 meters long is running at a speed of 54 km/h. How many seconds will it take to pass a bridge 250 meters long?
solutionStepByStep: Step 1: Total distance to be covered = Length of Train + Length of Bridge = 150 + 250 = 400 meters.

Step 2: Convert speed from km/h to m/s:
  - Speed = 54 * (5/18) = 3 * 5 = 15 m/s.
Step 3: Time taken = Total Distance / Speed = 400 / 15 = 80 / 3 = 26.67 seconds.
workedExamples.cuetInsight: Always add platform/bridge length to train length; never omit train's own physical length.

practiceQuestions.question: A motorist travels from Town A to Town B at 60 km/h and returns at 40 km/h. What is his average speed for the entire round trip?
A can finish a work in 15 days and B in 20 days. If they work together on it for 4 days, then the fraction of the work that is left is:
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Total work = LCM(15, 20) = 60 units.
Efficiency of A = 4 units/day; Efficiency of B = 3 units/day.
Together in 4 days = 4 * (4 + 3) = 28 units.
Work left = 60 - 28 = 32 units.
Fraction left = 32 / 60 = 8 / 15.

practiceQuestions.question: A man can row upstream at 8 km/h and downstream at 14 km/h. What is the speed of the man in still water and the rate of current?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Speed in still water = (Downstream + Upstream) / 2 = (14 + 8) / 2 = 11 km/h.
Rate of current = (Downstream - Upstream) / 2 = (14 - 8) / 2 = 3 km/h.

practiceQuestions.question: The average weight of 8 persons increases by 2.5 kg when a new person comes in place of one of them weighing 65 kg. What is the weight of the new person?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Total increase in weight = 8 * 2.5 = 20 kg.
Weight of new person = Replaced weight + Total increase = 65 + 20 = 85 kg.

practiceQuestions.question:
Assertion (A): Two trains of lengths 100m and 150m moving in opposite directions at 36 km/h and 54 km/h cross each other in 10 seconds.
Reason (R): Relative speed in opposite directions = 36 + 54 = 90 km/h = 90 * (5/18) = 25 m/s. Total distance = 100 + 150 = 250m. Time = 250 / 25 = 10 seconds.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)

practiceQuestions.explanation: Relative speed adds in opposite directions: 25 m/s. Total distance to cross is the sum of both train lengths: 250m. Time = 250 / 25 = 10s. Both are true and (R) explains (A).

practiceQuestions.question:
Match List-I (Speed in km/h) with List-II (Speed in m/s):
(P) 36 km/h — 1. 10 m/s
(Q) 54 km/h — 2. 15 m/s
(R) 72 km/h — 3. 20 m/s
(S) 90 km/h — 4. 25 m/s
Two pipes A and B can fill a tank in 20 minutes and 30 minutes respectively. If both pipes are opened together, the time taken to fill the tank is:
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Total capacity = LCM(20, 30) = 60 units.
Efficiency of A = 3 units/min; Efficiency of B = 2 units/min.
Combined efficiency = 3 + 2 = 5 units/min.
Time = 60 / 5 = 12 minutes.

practiceQuestions.question: The average of five consecutive numbers is 27. What is the largest of these numbers?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
For an odd count of consecutive numbers, the average is the middle number.
Middle number (3rd) = 27.
Numbers are 25, 26, 27, 28, 29.
The largest number is 29.

practiceQuestions.question: A person walks at 4 km/h instead of 3 km/h and covers 2 km more in the same time. What was the actual distance traveled at 3 km/h?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Let time be t hours. Distance at 4 km/h = 4t. Distance at 3 km/h = 3t.
4t - 3t = 2 km -> t = 2 hours.
Actual distance traveled at 3 km/h = 3 * 2 = 6 km.

practiceQuestions.question: A and B can complete a task together in 10 days. A alone can do it in 15 days. In how many days can B alone complete the task?
practiceQuestions.explanation:
Total work = LCM(10, 15) = 30 units.
Efficiency of (A + B) = 3 units/day. Efficiency of A = 2 units/day.
Efficiency of B = 3 - 2 = 1 unit/day.
Time taken by B alone = 30 / 1 = 30 days.
